output.name: Aluthe — the Lamp-Petrel
output.myth: Storm-petrels nest in the cracks of the north cliff, where no fox can reach, and their chicks are dark and quiet. Old Hesk the Reel counted them every autumn with a knot in her cord. One year Tavo the Gale came up the cliff in a black wind and tore the nest open, and the chicks went up the wind like sparks off a fire. Hesk counted and found one short. The last was smallest and had not learned to fly. Aun saw it turning above the rocks. He had cut one string and would not cut another. Kestal, the Loosed Gull, hangs high above the north cliff and calls down that a thing hauled from the dark is not always a catch. So Aun lit a lamp from his own kite and gave it to the chick. Tesmal, the Gull That Stays, hangs on her string to the east, the only one who never left. Now the chicks glow in flight. In a gale, a soft cluster of lights over the cliff is the nest still counting. Mirath is the last one, the one that was short.
output.finding: Find Kestal, the Loosed Gull, high in the north sky, then look a fist and a half straight south of it for Aluthe, the Lamp-Petrel.
